photos.question: The nurse is teaching a client to self-inject enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe. Which instruction is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #273!

💉 One tiny bubble in this syringe is supposed to be there. Do you know why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Do not expel the air bubble

🧠 Rationale: Enoxaparin is a low molecular weight heparin.

The air bubble in the prefilled syringe helps make sure the full dose is given.

Do not aspirate or rub the site, since both increase bruising.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Enoxaparin

💊 Drug Class: Low molecular weight heparin

❤️ Primary Use: Prevent and treat DVT and PE

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Bleeding and bruising

🔹 Low platelets

🔹 Injection site pain

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Inject in the abdomen, 2 inches from the navel

✅ Rotate sites

✅ Do not rub the site

✅ Report black stools or unusual bleeding

🚑 Antidote: Protamine sulfate (partial reversal)

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Keep the bubble, skip the rub!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which finding should the nurse expect in a client with left-sided heart failure?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #274!

❤️ Left side or right side? This one trips up so many students!

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Crackles in the lungs

🧠 Rationale: When the left ventricle fails, blood backs up into the lungs.

This causes crackles, dyspnea and orthopnea.

JVD, ascites and an enlarged liver point to right-sided failure.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Left-Sided Heart Failure

🫁 Where Fluid Goes: Back into the lungs

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Crackles

🔹 Dyspnea and orthopnea

🔹 Pink frothy sputum (severe)

🔹 Fatigue

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ High Fowler position

✅ Give oxygen as ordered

✅ Give diuretics as ordered

✅ Daily weights and strict I and O

🚑 Escalate: Pink frothy sputum or sudden worsening dyspnea

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Left = Lungs. Right = Rest of the body.

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #HeartFailure #CardiacNursing #MedSurg #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Which finding should the nurse expect in a client with hypothyroidism?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #275!

🦋 Everything slows down with this thyroid problem. Can you spot it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Cold intolerance and weight gain

🧠 Rationale: Hypothyroidism slows the body's metabolism.

Clients feel cold, gain weight and feel tired.

Heat intolerance, weight loss and tremors point to hyperthyroidism.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hypothyroidism

🧬 Problem: Too little thyroid hormone

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Cold intolerance

🔹 Weight gain

🔹 Fatigue and constipation

🔹 Slow heart rate

🔹 Dry skin and hair loss

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Give levothyroxine every morning on an empty stomach

✅ Keep the client warm

✅ Watch for chest pain when starting thyroid hormone

🚑 Emergency: Myxedema coma, with low temp, low BP and confusion

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Hypo = everything goes LOW and SLOW.

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which toy is best for a hospitalized 2-year-old?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #276!

🧸 Picking the right toy is a real NCLEX skill. Which one would you hand a toddler?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Push-pull toy

🧠 Rationale: Toddlers learn through movement and are in the autonomy stage.

Push-pull toys build gross motor skills.

Small pieces are a choking risk, and rule-based games fit school-age children.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Toddler Growth and Development

👶 Age: 1 to 3 years

🧠 Erikson Stage: Autonomy vs shame and doubt

🎈 Type of Play: Parallel play

✅ Good Toys:

🔹 Push-pull toys

🔹 Large blocks

🔹 Stacking toys

🔹 Large crayons

⚠️ Safety:

✅ No small parts, coins or balloons

✅ Avoid grapes and hot dogs unless cut small

🚑 Choking risk is highest in this age group

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Toddlers on the go need toys that go!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Why should a client planning a pregnancy take folic acid?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #277!

🤰 This vitamin protects the baby before many people even know they are pregnant!

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — To prevent neural tube defects

🧠 Rationale: Folic acid lowers the risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida.

The neural tube forms very early, often before a client knows she is pregnant.

That is why folic acid is started before conception.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Folic Acid in Pregnancy

💊 Supplement: Folic acid (vitamin B9)

❤️ Purpose: Prevent neural tube defects

📏 Usual Dose: 400 mcg daily for most clients

🥬 Food Sources:

🔹 Leafy green vegetables

🔹 Fortified cereals

🔹 Beans and lentils

🔹 Citrus fruits

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Start at least 1 month before pregnancy

✅ Continue through early pregnancy

🚑 Higher Dose: Clients with a prior neural tube defect pregnancy, as ordered

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Folic acid = Fold the neural tube right!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #OBNursing #Pregnancy #PrenatalCare #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client says, "I can't stop shaking and I don't know why." Which response by the nurse is best?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #278!

🧠 Therapeutic communication questions are all over the NCLEX. Pick the best response!

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — You seem anxious. Tell me what you are feeling.

🧠 Rationale: Naming what the nurse sees and inviting the client to share is therapeutic.

False reassurance and changing the subject block communication.

Why questions can make clients feel defensive.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Therapeutic Communication

✅ Therapeutic Techniques:

🔹 Making observations

🔹 Open-ended questions

🔹 Reflecting feelings

🔹 Silence

⚠️ Nontherapeutic Responses:

🔹 False reassurance

🔹 Asking why

🔹 Changing the subject

🔹 Giving advice

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Stay with the anxious client

✅ Use short, calm sentences

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Focus on FEELINGS, not fixing.

photos.question: A client with long-term COPD has clubbing of the fingers. What does this finding suggest?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #279!

🫁 The fingertips can tell you a lot about the lungs. Do you know this sign?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Long-term low oxygen levels

🧠 Rationale: Clubbing develops slowly from chronic hypoxia.

It is common in COPD, cystic fibrosis and some heart defects.

It does not appear suddenly with an acute infection.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Clubbing and Chronic Hypoxia

🔍 What It Looks Like: Rounded, enlarged fingertips and nail beds

⚠️ Common Causes:

🔹 COPD

🔹 Cystic fibrosis

🔹 Congenital heart defects

🔹 Lung cancer

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Assess oxygen saturation

✅ Check for cyanosis and dyspnea

✅ Give oxygen as ordered

🚑 Escalate: New or rapidly worsening hypoxia

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Clubbing = Chronic low oxygen.
